fact: On January 26, 1950, the Constitution of India came into effect, replacing the Government of India Act. This is why we celebrate Republic Day on January 26 every year.
India has over 1,55,000 post offices — the world's largest postal network. More than 89% of them are in rural areas, serving as the backbone of communication for millions of Indians.
On May 29, 1953, Tenzing Norgay and Edmund Hillary became the first people to summit Mount Everest. Tenzing, who lived in Darjeeling, India, received the George Medal for this achievement.
The Mahakumbh Mela at Prayagraj is the largest peaceful human gathering on Earth. Held every 12 years, the 2025 edition attracted over 40 crore visitors in just 45 days.
The Ganga originates from the Gangotri Glacier in the Himalayas and flows 2,525 kilometres before meeting the Bay of Bengal. It is the most sacred river in Hinduism.
India held its first general election in 1951–52 with 17.32 crore voters — the largest democratic exercise in history at that time. Voter turnout was 45.7% across 489 constituencies.
On June 2, 2014, Telangana officially became India's 29th state, carved out from the northern and northwestern regions of Andhra Pradesh, with Hyderabad as its capital.
World Environment Day has been celebrated on June 5 since 1973. India hosted the 2018 edition with the theme 'Beat Plastic Pollution', highlighting India's commitment to environmental action.
India's Western Ghats — also called the Sahyadri Range — is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the world's 8 most important biodiversity hotspots, stretching 1,600 km along the west coast.
World Environment Day is June 5. India is home to the world's largest mangrove forest — the Sundarbans — and is one of only 17 'megadiverse' countries on Earth.
ISRO was founded on August 15, 1969 with Dr. Vikram Sarabhai as its founding father. India's Chandrayaan-3 made India the first country to land near the Moon's south pole in 2023.
India has the world's third-largest railway network, covering over 68,000 km of track. Indian Railways carries about 23 million passengers every day — more than the entire population of Australia.
On June 9, 1540, Maharana Pratap was born. He was the great Rajput king of Mewar who famously fought against Mughal emperor Akbar at the Battle of Haldighati in 1576.
India produces over 20 million tonnes of mangoes per year — about 40% of global production. The mango is India's national fruit and the country grows over 1,000 varieties of it.
India's Constitution is the world's longest written national constitution, with 448 articles, 25 parts, 12 schedules, and 5 appendices. It took 2 years, 11 months, and 18 days to draft.
The Sundarbans, shared between India and Bangladesh, is the world's largest mangrove delta and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. It is the only mangrove forest in the world inhabited by tigers.
India is among the world's top tea producers, growing about 1.3 million tonnes per year. Assam produces more tea than any other region in India, followed by West Bengal's famous Darjeeling.
The Indian Peacock was declared India's national bird in 1963. The male's colourful fan of feathers, called a 'train', can span up to 1.8 metres. It is found across the Indian subcontinent.

India is the world's largest producer of milk, producing over 230 million tonnes per year. The White Revolution (Operation Flood), started in 1970, transformed India into the world's top dairy nation.
The Tropic of Cancer passes through 8 Indian states: Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura, and Mizoram.
India has the world's largest film industry by number of films produced. Bollywood produces over 1,800 films per year, and Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, and Malayalam industries add thousands more.
The River Brahmaputra is one of the world's longest rivers and Asia's largest river by discharge. It flows from Tibet into Arunachal Pradesh, then through Assam, before entering Bangladesh.
India's Aadhaar system, launched in 2009, is the world's largest biometric ID system. It has enrolled over 1.39 billion people, assigning each a unique 12-digit identification number.

India gained independence from British rule on August 15, 1947. Jawaharlal Nehru delivered his famous 'Tryst with Destiny' speech at midnight, making it one of the most celebrated speeches in history.
Children's Day (Bal Diwas) is celebrated on November 14, the birthday of Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru, India's first Prime Minister. He was fondly called 'Chacha Nehru' by children across India.
